params.label: Guidance
params.help: How hard the model is pushed to match your prompt. Low wanders off the brief but tends to sound relaxed and natural; high follows the words closely and can turn harsh or lifeless. The default is the value this model was tuned around.

params.label: Temperature
params.help: How adventurous the model is at each step. Lower is safer and more repetitive; higher is more surprising and more likely to wander or fall apart. What counts as high differs between models, so move away from the default in small steps.

params.label: Top-K
params.help: At each step the model considers only its K likeliest options. Small keeps it tight and predictable; large lets rarer, stranger sounds through. Temperature then chooses among whatever this leaves.

params.label: Seed
params.help: The random starting point. The same seed with the same prompt and settings reproduces a take exactly, which is how you change one setting and hear only that change. Leave it on Random for something different every run.

params.label: Steps

params.label: Guidance
params.help: How hard the model is pushed to match your prompt. Low wanders off the brief but tends to sound relaxed and natural; high follows the words closely and can turn harsh or lifeless. The default is the value this model was tuned around.

params.label: LM reasoning
params.help: A language model drafts the arrangement — sections, instrumentation, where the vocal sits — before the audio model renders it. Slower, and usually more coherent across a long track.

params.label: BPM
params.help: Target tempo in beats per minute. Left on Random the model picks one to suit the prompt. It is a request rather than a guarantee — nothing locks the output to a click.

params.label: Vocal language
params.help: Which language the model should sing in. Write the lyrics in that language too: this tells the model how to pronounce them, it does not translate.

params.label: Seed
params.help: The random starting point. The same seed with the same prompt and settings reproduces a take exactly, which is how you change one setting and hear only that change. Leave it on Random for something different every run.

params.label: Task
params.help: What to do with the source audio (if any).

params.label: Source audio
params.help: Required for every task except Generate; output length locks to this file.

params.label: Style reference
params.help: Optional style reference for Cover.

params.label: Source strength
params.help: How strongly the source shapes the result — lower (0.2) is closer to pure style transfer. Applies to every task that takes a source, not only Cover.

params.label: Morph
params.help: Rewrite the source from one description into another (FlowEdit). Needs a source audio file; works on the Turbo DiT, unlike extract/layer/complete.

params.label: Source description
params.placeholder: e.g. upbeat electropop with a female vocal
params.help: What the source is now — a morph travels from this description to the prompt. Left empty it morphs away from nothing in particular, which blurs the result.

params.label: Repaint start (s)
params.help: Where the regenerated span starts, in seconds from the beginning of the source. Audio outside the span is kept exactly as it was.

params.label: Repaint end (s)
params.help: Where the regenerated span ends, in seconds. -1 means to the end of the track.

params.label: Key
params.help: The key to write in, such as 'F minor' or 'C major'. Left blank the model chooses one to suit the description.

params.label: Time signature
params.help: The time signature, such as '4' for four-four or '3' for waltz time. Left blank the model chooses.

params.label: Model picks tempo & key
params.help: Let the planner choose the tempo, key and time signature. Turn it off and it uses only what you have set, leaving anything blank to the renderer.

params.label: Model rewrites the description
params.help: Let the planner rewrite your description into its own words before rendering. Often an improvement; turn it off when you have worded the prompt carefully.

params.label: Model detects the language
params.help: Let the planner work out which language the lyrics are in, rather than taking the language you set.

params.label: Planner variety
params.help: How adventurous the planner is when it decides the tempo, key and shape of the song. Lower gives you the obvious reading of your description; higher takes more interesting and less predictable decisions.

params.label: Planner guidance
params.help: How closely the planner sticks to your description when it writes the plan. Higher follows your words more literally; lower lets it fill in more of its own.

params.label: Planner nucleus
params.help: How much of the planner's vocabulary stays in play at each step. Below 1.0 it ignores its least likely choices, which makes the plan safer and more conventional.

params.help: A short recording of the voice this should become — your own, or one you have permission to use. Ten clean seconds is plenty.

params.label: Steps
params.help: Diffusion passes. 30 is the upstream default; more refines the timbre and takes proportionally longer.

params.label: Copy style
params.help: Also carry the reference's emotion, accent and delivery — not just the timbre.

params.label: Anonymize only
params.help: Strip the speaker's identity instead of imitating the reference — the output is a neutral voice.

params.label: Voice similarity
params.help: How hard the conversion is pushed toward the reference voice — higher is a closer imitation.

params.label: Clarity
params.help: How hard the words are held onto — raise it if the conversion mumbles, lower it for a looser read.

params.label: Length stretch
params.help: Stretch factor of the converted performance — below 1 speeds the delivery up, above 1 slows it down.

models.notes: Runs on CPU, about 6× the clip length at 30 steps (measured). The reference voice is supplied per job and never stored. The V2 stack (AR + CFM, ~3 GB with its content extractors) auto-fetches on the first conversion.

models.description: Types words, sings them: zero-shot singing voice synthesis. Give it a melody (a sung or played line, or a MIDI file), the lyrics, and a few seconds of the voice that should perform them — your own recording works. Bilingual Chinese/English.

params.label: Source audio
params.help: The melody to sing — a vocal or single-line instrumental recording the singer follows.

params.label: Melody (MIDI)
params.help: A MIDI melody instead of the recording — wins when both are set.

params.label: Voice reference
params.help: A short clean recording of the voice that should sing — yours, or one you have permission to use.

params.label: Reference words
params.placeholder: the words spoken/sung in the reference clip
params.help: What the reference recording actually says or sings — the model needs the text to read the voice.

params.label: Lyrics
params.help: The words to perform to the melody.

params.label: Steps
params.help: Diffusion passes. 8 is the proven fast setting; 32 is upstream's quality default.

params.label: Guidance
params.help: How hard the singer is held to the lyrics and melody. Higher is more literal and can strain; lower is looser and more natural.

params.label: Pitch shift (semitones)
params.help: Transpose the melody into the reference voice's comfortable range.

models.notes: The voice is supplied per job and never stored — no voice library ships with this app, deliberately. Chinese-centric training; English works, judge it by ear. The SDPA attention substitute ignores their sliding window — restoring it is the known quality follow-up.

models.description: Scores a track against vocabularies of genres, moods and instruments and keeps the labels that fit. No tagging model is trained or downloaded — it is the same CLAP encoder that powers timbre matching, asked a different question.

params.label: Source audio
params.help: The audio to tag.

params.label: Tags per group
params.help: How many labels to keep for each of genre, mood and instrumentation.

models.notes: Zero-shot: the vocabulary is the model. Labels it has never been trained on still score, and niche genres score poorly.

models.description: TRAINED tags rather than zero-shot: MTG's Discogs-EffNet embeds the track once, then tiny heads score 400 Discogs genre styles, a dozen mood-and-character axes (happy/sad/party/aggressive/relaxed, acoustic/electronic, bright or dark timbre, tonal/atonal, approachability, engagement), danceability and voice/instrumental. Seconds per song — the embedding is cached, so re-tagging and library sweeps cost almost nothing. Weights (~25 MB) fetch from UPF on first run.

params.label: Source audio
params.help: The audio to tag.

params.label: Genres to keep
params.help: How many of the 400 genre styles to keep, best first; moods and danceability report on their own thresholds.

models.notes: Non-commercial: MTG licenses the models CC BY-NC-SA and offers commercial terms on request. The 400-style genre vocabulary is Discogs's own taxonomy — expect precise electronic-music subgenres in particular.

models.description: Writes down the words as sung, with a timing on every line. Quantised small enough to stay loaded alongside a music model rather than displacing it — run it on a separated vocal for a transcript rather than a guess.

params.label: Source audio

params.label: Language
params.help: Two-letter code (en, fr, ja). Left blank the model detects it, which is usually right and occasionally confident and wrong.

models.notes: Whisper is a speech model: given music with no words in it, it invents some. Lines it had no confidence in are dropped, so an instrumental usually comes back empty rather than wrong — but run it on a vocal and it is a transcript.

models.description: The same model unquantised: a little more accurate on quiet or crowded vocals, and large enough that loading it unloads whatever music model was resident.

models.description: The annotation model behind ACE-Step 1.5's training data: a Qwen2.5-Omni fine-tune that transcribes SUNG words — 50+ languages — and marks the song's structure inline ([Verse], [Chorus], [Spoken Word Intro]). Where Whisper guesses at singing, this was trained on it.

params.label: Source audio
params.help: The audio to transcribe — full mixes are fine; this model was trained on them.

params.label: Length limit
params.help: How long the transcript may run before it is cut off — long songs need headroom.

models.description: The other half of ACE-Step's annotation pair: listens to a track and writes an unusually precise production-level description — genre, groove, instrumentation, mix character. Also answers a typed question about the audio.

models.description: The conversational music expert: an 8B audio-language model that answers real musicology questions — key, tempo, chord movement, arrangement, production choices — with visible reasoning behind them. Also transcribes sung lyrics on request. MLX-native: loads in a second.

params.label: Source audio

models.description: Stanford's symbolic composer: writes MIDI note events directly (no audio model in the loop), which the note renderer then voices. Its actual specialty is working WITH existing notes: continue a part from where it stops, or fill a gap in the middle while respecting what comes after.

params.label: Mode
params.help: Continue picks up where the MIDI part stops; fill-a-gap rewrites only the window below, keeping the notes on both sides. Both need a MIDI file; the result always includes the input notes.

params.label: Notes to extend
params.help: The MIDI part to continue or fill — a transcription or an earlier composition both work.

params.label: Gap start (s)
params.help: Fill-a-gap only: where the rewritten window begins.

params.label: Gap end (s)
params.help: Fill-a-gap only: where the window ends — the notes after it are kept and respected.

params.label: Length (s)
params.help: How many seconds of music to compose (from-nothing and continue). Time is musical output length, not render time.

params.label: Top-P
params.help: At each step the model considers only its likeliest options, up to this share of the total probability — 0.9 keeps the top 90%. A softer Top-K: how many options stay in play rises and falls with how certain the model is.

models.notes: Ignores the prompt — generation is unconditional over MIDI events. Token-by-token and slow on CPU (~23 min for 10 s in triage); the adapter tries MPS first, which should recover ~10×.

params.help: How adventurous the model is at each step. Lower is safer and more repetitive; higher is more surprising and more likely to wander or fall apart. What counts as high differs between models, so move away from the default in small steps.
